entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Krishan Pahal,J.
1.
2. Heard Sri Shivam Singh, learned counsel for applicant and Sri R.P. Patel, learned A.G.A. for the State.
3. This is the third bail application on behalf of applicant.
The first two bail applications were rejected vide orders dated 21.1.2019 and 8.10.2020 by this Court.

4. The present bail application has been filed by the applicant in Case Crime No. 185 of 2018, under Section 376-D IPC and Section 6 POCSO Act, Police Station Bhuta, District Bareilly with the prayer to enlarge him on bail.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
5. Learned counsel for the applicant has stated that an FIR was lodged against the informant by the family members of the applicant and the present FIR is a counterblast to the FIR lodged in the year,
2016.
Learned counsel has further stated that the applicant has no criminal antecedents to his credit.
The applicant is incarcerated in jail since 8.7.2018.

6. Per contra, learned A.G.A. has vehemently opposed the bail application on the ground that there is no any new ground for granting bail except long period of incarceration i.e. four and a half years.

7. After hearing learned counsel for the parties, going through the record and taking into consideration that no new ground is there for pressing the bail except long period of incarceration, I do not find it a fit case for grant of bail to the applicant.
8. The bail application is found devoid of merits and is, accordingly, dismissed.

9. However, it is directed that the court below may proceed with the trial and reach at the logical conclusion expeditiously, if there is no legal impediment, within a period of six months from the date of production of a certified copy of this order.

10. It is clarified that the observations made herein are limited to the facts brought in by the parties pertaining to the disposal of bail application and the said observations shall have no bearing on the merits of the case during trial.
